title: Cycles and chaos in a socialist economy
journal: Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control
summary_en: Can a planned economy generate endogenous business cycles — and even chaos — purely from its planning rules? Hommes, Nusse and Simonovits build a stylised dynamic model of a centrally-planned ('socialist') economy with adaptive output targets and show that the resulting investment cycle can exhibit endogenous oscillations and chaotic dynamics for plausible parameter ranges. The paper formalised long-running narrative claims (Kornai-style) about cyclical dysfunction under central planning into a rigorous nonlinear-dynamics framework.
data_used: Theoretical / numerical paper. Numerical illustrations use stylised Hungarian and Eastern-European socialist-era output series; formal results derive from the planning-rule dynamic system.
policy_relevance: Of historical interest for Hungarian transition-economics scholarship (KRTK, Corvinus economic history) — the paper formalises the cyclical-dysfunction story of late-socialist planning in Hungary and the bloc, which informs comparative-economic-systems teaching and analyses of pre-1989 Hungarian growth volatility.
